inlineContent.text: EnsemblesEncrypted provides
, a wrapper that encrypts files before uploading and decrypts after downloading. It can wrap any
implementation — CloudKit, Google Drive, WebDAV, or your own custom backend — to provide end-to-end encryption for sync data.
Encrypted files are stored in a password-derived vault directory with a
extension. This is backward compatible with the Ensembles 2 Objective-C
Two encryption formats are available:
(default) — AES-256-GCM. Fast, authenticated encryption using Apple’s CryptoKit. Recommended for new apps.
— RNCryptor v3 format. Use this for backward compatibility with Ensembles 2 encrypted data.
The backend auto-detects the encryption format when downloading, so a
client can read
files and vice versa. The format setting only controls how
new
files are encrypted.

Ensembles sync data is stored as opaque binary files, so even without encryption the raw data is not human-readable. However, it could be deserialized by someone with access to your cloud storage.
For
CloudKit
, Apple encrypts
data at rest. With Advanced Data Protection (ADP) enabled, assets are end-to-end encrypted. Wrapping CloudKit with
adds a layer of protection that doesn’t depend on the user enabling ADP.
For
third-party backends
(Google Drive, OneDrive, WebDAV, etc.), the storage provider can see the raw files. Wrapping with
ensures data is encrypted before it leaves the device, regardless of what the provider does.
Vault directory

— All encrypted files are stored inside a vault directory in the cloud, derived from the password. Different passwords create different vaults, so the same cloud account can host multiple independent encrypted sync stores.
Upload
— When Ensembles uploads a file, the wrapper encrypts it to a local temporary file, uploads the encrypted version with a
extension, then removes the temporary file.
Download
— When Ensembles downloads a file, the wrapper downloads the encrypted
file, auto-detects the format (modern or legacy), decrypts it to a local temporary file, and returns the decrypted content.
Backward compatibility
— The
format uses RNCryptor v3, the same encryption format used by Ensembles 2’s
. Apps migrating from E2 to E3 can read existing encrypted cloud data without re-encrypting.
